artists.biography: After the Zombies broke up, keyboardist/songwriter Rod Argent formed his own band in 1969, which incorporated more classical, jazz, and art rock influences in accordance with Argent's musical training. The group's other members were guitarist/songwriter Russ Ballard, bassist Jim Rodford, and drummer Bob Henrit. Argent's first two albums, Argent and Ring of Hands, received a fair amount of critical acclaim, but their real breakthrough came with 1972's All Together Now, which contained the Top Five smash "Hold Your Head Up"; In Deep produced a minor hit in "God Gave Rock 'N' Roll to You," which was covered by Kiss in 1992. By 1974, Ballard had developed his songwriting talents enough to leave for a solo career (Three Dog Night had a Top Ten single in 1971 with his "Liar," from Argent), and was replaced by guitarist John Verity and string player John Grimaldi. Without Ballard, the group lost its focus and indulged its tendencies toward extended art rock passages and improvisational solos to somewhat excessive levels. Argent broke up in 1976; Rodford joined the Kinks, while Argent himself recorded several solo albums and became a record producer, working with Tanita Tikaram, among others.

The group's other members were guitarist/songwriter Russ Ballard, bassist Jim Rodford, and drummer Bob Henrit. Argent's first two albums, Argent and Ring of Hands, received a fair amount of critical acclaim, but their real breakthrough came with 1972's All Together Now, which contained the Top Five smash "Hold Your Head Up"; In Deep produced a minor hit in "God Gave Rock 'N' Roll to You," which was covered by Kiss in 1992. By 1974, Ballard had developed his songwriting talents enough to leave for a solo career (Three Dog Night had a Top Ten single in 1971 with his "Liar," from Argent), and was replaced by guitarist John Verity and string player John Grimaldi. Without Ballard, the group lost its focus and indulged its tendencies toward extended art rock passages and improvisational solos to somewhat excessive levels. Argent broke up in 1976; Rodford joined the Kinks, while Argent himself recorded several solo albums and became a record producer, working with Tanita Tikaram, among others.

perplexity.description:
Hold Your Head Up - The Best Of Argent is a compilation album by the English rock band Argent, originally released in 1997 by Demon Records. The album showcases the band’s signature blend of melodic rock, progressive elements, and keyboard-driven arrangements, highlighting their most memorable tracks from the early 1970s. Argent’s sound is defined by Rod Argent’s inventive Hammond organ work and the band’s knack for crafting catchy, riff-based songs, with the title track “Hold Your Head Up” standing as their most iconic hit—a Top 5 success in both the US and UK and a gold-certified single.

This compilation serves as a concise introduction to Argent’s discography, capturing their peak years and their only major chart success in the United States. While the band explored progressive rock and hard rock on their studio albums, Hold Your Head Up - The Best Of Argent emphasizes their accessible, radio-friendly singles and enduring anthems. The album was well-received by fans and critics for its selection of highlights, including the celebrated organ solo on “Hold Your Head Up,” which has been praised as one of the greatest in rock history. It remains a definitive collection of Argent’s most influential work.
